verdict.rationale: GitHub's fine-grained personal access tokens let a user grant a specific, minimal set of permissions per resource, and the REST API even returns an X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions header showing exactly what scope is required for an endpoint — a direct implementation of least-privilege credentialing that any automated actor (including an agent) can use to authenticate to the API. Missing for 10: explicit documentation tying fine-grained PAT/GitHub App scoping specifically to Copilot/agent workflows (e.g., an agent-specific token-issuance flow) and independent hands-on confirmation.
